mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has risen in each of the last four weekly means (-20.0, -17.9, -15.0, -14.3), which restores commuting routines and weekday lunchtime and after-work footfall in retail-and-recreation districts; continued commuting recovery therefore lifts RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks above its trailing 28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose in each of the four weekly means ending t-0w
failure_condition: WORKPLACES continues to rise for the next four weekly means while the next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is less than or equal to -19.0 (its trailing 28-day mean).

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has declined monotonically (7.4, 5.3, 4.1, 3.7), meaning the share of time spent at home is shrinking; each further decline of one point in RESIDENTIAL releases discretionary out-of-home trips, so RETAIL_REC rises over the following four weeks relative to the trailing four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 7.4 at t-3w to 3.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL falls below 3.0 in the next four weekly means while the next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC stays at or below -19.0.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station mobility has recovered steadily (-24.1, -20.3, -16.6, -15.7) and transit is the modal gateway to Tokyo retail districts; as TRANSIT closes on its baseline, destination retail trips increase, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next two weeks than a continuation of the current level would imply.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 8.4 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: TRANSIT remains above -17 for the next two weekly means while RETAIL_REC fails to exceed -16.4 in either of those weeks.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC recovery is gated jointly by commuting and transit capacity: retail footfall only accelerates when WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both recover in the same week, because commuter-derived demand requires both a trip purpose and an available trip. The joint condition holds in all four observed weeks, so RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rose in each of the last three week-over-week comparisons
failure_condition: In weeks where WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise, RETAIL_REC nonetheless falls, or the next-28-day RETAIL_REC mean is at or below -19.0.

mechanism_narrative: Once TRANSIT crosses above -15.0 percent of baseline it signals that capacity restrictions on public transport have eased enough for discretionary non-commute trips; the crossing releases pent-up leisure-retail demand and produces a step-up in RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks beyond the pre-crossing trend.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean rises above -15.0 percent of baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT stands at -15.7 at t-0w, 0.7 points below the -15.0 threshold
failure_condition: TRANSIT exceeds -15.0 in the next two weekly means and RETAIL_REC does not exceed its t-0w value of -16.4 within two weeks of the crossing.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM remains 9 points above baseline while RETAIL_REC is 16 points below, indicating households still concentrate spending on provisioning and minimize browsing-type trips. Persistent grocery-and-pharmacy elevation above 8 therefore keeps discretionary retail suppressed and pushes the next-28-day RETAIL_REC mean below the trailing 28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM averaged 8.0 or higher in the last three weekly means while RETAIL_REC stayed below -16
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM stays above 8.0 for the next four weekly means while the next-28-day RETAIL_REC mean exceeds -19.0.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility spiked to 8.4 and then fell to 4.7 while RETAIL_REC rose only modestly, showing that outdoor recreation is substituting for indoor retail-and-recreation visits during the late-winter period; a PARKS level above 4 keeps that substitution active and holds the short-horizon retail direction down over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean above 4.0 percent of baseline
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS peaked at 8.4 at t-1w as RETAIL_REC gained only 1.2 points to -16.4
failure_condition: PARKS remains above 4.0 for the next weekly mean while RETAIL_REC rises above -15.0 over that same week.

mechanism_narrative: Under the current reopening regime, defined by RESIDENTIAL falling and WORKPLACES recovering simultaneously, restrictions are being relaxed rather than reimposed; the relaxation path mechanically lifts retail-and-recreation visits, so RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks exceeds its trailing 28-day mean provided RESIDENTIAL keeps declining.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean declines for two consecutive weeks while WORKPLACES rises
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell in each of the last three weeks while WORKPLACES rose in each of them
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL declines and WORKPLACES rises for two more consecutive weeks, yet the next-28-day RETAIL_REC mean is at or below -19.0.
